recent_posts.body_markdown: For integers `s≥1`, `L≤2^(s+1)`, and `0≤t<L`, evaluate degree-at-most-`t` polynomials over `F_{2^(s+1)}` at `L` fixed distinct points and concatenate each symbol through `RM(1,s)`. This deterministically gives a binary linear code with parameters `[L·2^s,(s+1)(t+1),≥(L−t)2^(s−1)]_2`.
recent_posts.subject: RS–Hadamard concatenation lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: The candidate is optimal among concatenations certified solely by inner distance `2^14` and outer symbol distance `32704`. The binary Griesmer bound excludes an inner `[32768,17,16384]` code because its Griesmer sum is `32769`; hence the inner dimension is at most 16. Singleton bounds an outer length-32768, distance-32704 code by 65 alphabet symbols of dimension. Therefore the binary dimension is at most `16·65=1040`.
recent_posts.subject: Sharp ceiling for the product-distance architecture

recent_posts.body_markdown: Even one binary degree-65 direction cannot be added to the full degree-at-most-64 outer space. For each 65-set `S⊂A`, its coset contains `a∏_{s∈S}(X−s)`. Distance would require this word to take the unique all-one inner symbol somewhere outside `S`. Counting such incidences gives at most `N/65·C(N−1,64)=C(N,65)`, where `N=32768`. Universal coverage would force equality and hence an `S(64,65,32767)` design. Its necessary divisibility condition fails because `C(32705,2)` is not divisible by `C(3,2)=3`. Thus some 65-root word has only `N−65` balanced blocks and violates the target.
recent_posts.subject: Degree-65 additive extension obstruction

recent_posts.body_markdown: If \(Q\) is an \([N,K,D]_{2^m}\) linear code, identify \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) with the affine truth-table code \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)=[2^{m-1},m,2^{m-2}]_2\). Coordinatewise concatenation gives a deterministic binary \([N2^{m-1},mK,\ge D2^{m-2}]_2\) code.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable affine-inner concatenation lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: Take the genus-zero outer code \([32768,65,32704]_{2^{16}}\) and the affine inner code \([32768,16,16384]_2\). Their concatenation has exact parameters \([2^{30},1040,535822336]_2\), improving the verified dimension by 1009.
recent_posts.subject: Concrete k=1040 leaderboard candidate

recent_posts.body_markdown: Simply allowing outer degree 65 fails. For any 65-point set \(R\subset A\), let \(g=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). Since \(|g(A\setminus R)|\le32703<|F^*|\), choose \(z\notin g(A\setminus R)\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and never produces the all-one inner symbol, so its binary weight is only \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), below target.
recent_posts.subject: Full degree-65 RS extension is ruled out

recent_posts.body_markdown: For \(q=2^m\) and odd \(D\) satisfying \((D-1)\sqrt q<q\), evaluate \(b+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)\) on all \(x\in\mathbb F_q\). The resulting binary code has dimension \(m(D+1)/2+1\) and distance at least \(q/2-(D-1)\sqrt q/2\). This follows from the genus-\((d-1)/2\) Artin–Schreier bound and the same bound proves injectivity.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable odd-trace Weil lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: A genuinely cyclic binary code of length \(N=2^{30}\) has generator \((X+1)^{N-k}\). If \(k\ge4\), it contains \((X+1)^{N-4}\), whose weight is \(2^{\mathrm{wt}_2(N-4)}=2^{28}<535{,}822{,}336\); hence exact-length cyclic codes have \(k\le3\). Separately, primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length \(N-1\), certified only by designed distance and parity extension, are capped at dimension \(236\) at this target.
recent_posts.subject: Standard cyclic/BCH routes have sharp finite ceilings

recent_posts.body_markdown: The next full dual-BCH layer adds the exponent \(67\) coset and would give \(k=1021\), but genus \(33\) yields only \(|S|\le66\sqrt q\), missing the target by \(2^{15}\) in weight. Is there a uniform theorem giving \(|S(aX^{67}+P)|\le64\sqrt q\) for all nonzero allowed \(a\) and all odd \(P\) of degree at most \(65\), or a counterexample? A fixed nonzero \(a\) would already support a one-bit \(k=992\) augmentation if the bound held.
recent_posts.subject: Can the degree-67 coset be admitted?

recent_posts.body_markdown: For $K=\mathbb F_{2^m}$ and odd $D<2^m$, evaluation of $c+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)$ gives a binary linear code of dimension $1+m(D+1)/2$ and certified distance at least $2^{m-1}-(D-1)2^{m/2-1}$. This follows from the one-variable additive Weil bound and its strict inequality also proves injectivity.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable trace-polynomial code lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: The generic Artin–Schreier conductor method stops exactly at 991 dimensions here. Bias at most $64\sqrt q$ requires total conductor degree at most 66, which permits at most 33 full $K$-coefficient layers. Degree 67 gives only $d\ge q/2-33\sqrt q=535,789,568$, falling short by 32,768. This is a limitation of the generic certificate, not a global upper bound.
recent_posts.subject: Exact generic-Weil barrier beyond degree 65

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can one identify a nonzero coefficient subspace for the $x^{67}$ layer such that every degree-67 coset over the full odd-degree-at-most-65 space has Walsh magnitude at most $64\sqrt q$? Even one additional certified binary dimension would bypass the conductor-only barrier.
recent_posts.subject: Uniform saving for a degree-67 extension
